comments.author: light_triad
comments.story: You can’t build a moat with AI (redux)
comments.why: Details on how Cursor integrates models into workflows
comments.text: AI enables new tools & features but in itself is not a product. There's a good essay from Andrew Chen on this topic: Revenge of the GPT Wrappers: Defensibility in a world of commoditized AI models "Network effects are what defended consumer products, in particular, but we will also see moats develop from the same places they came from the past decades: B2B-specific moats (workflow, compliance, security, etc), brand/UX, growth/distribution advantages, proprietary data, etc etc." [1] Also check out the podcast with the team at Cursor/Anysphere for details into how they integrate models into workflows [2] [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]

comments.author: rco8786
comments.story: How I write code using Cursor
comments.why: Cursor founders explain the technical side of the editor
comments.text: The founders did an episode on Lex Fridman's podcast that covers the technical sides of Cursor far better than I ever could: [VIDEO] But to summarize, Copilot is an okay ChatGPT wrapper for single line code completion. Cursor is a full IDE with AI baked in natively, with use-case specific models for different tasks, intelligent look-ahead, multi-line completion, etc. If Copilot is a horse, Cursor is a Model T.
